items.title: The Figma agent is now available in FigJam and Slides
items.excerpt: Figma extends its AI agent beyond Figma Design into FigJam and Slides, so it can help explore ideas on the whiteboard, prepare meetings and build presentations from design work.
items.rationale: Primary-source launch that puts the Figma agent into two more daily surfaces (FigJam whiteboarding, Slides decks) — immediately usable by designers tomorrow.

items.title: Framer adds Automations, Connectors and a Slack Agent to its design agent
items.excerpt: Framer's new Automations are agent workflows that run on a schedule or on project events like publishing or form submissions; Connectors let the Framer agent read and act in Slack, Notion and Ahrefs, and a Slack Agent can query the site, check analytics or make quick edits from Slack.
items.rationale: New Framer release turning its site agent into scheduled/event-driven automations with Slack, Notion and Ahrefs connectors — concrete new capability for web designers.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.excerpt: The NYT told its photographers to hold off on a Photoshop update because it does not want AI metadata inadvertently attached to its news photos.
items.rationale: A major newsroom halting a Photoshop update over AI provenance metadata is a fresh, practical warning for any image pro whose files carry content credentials.

items.title: Cognitive Design 2.3 marks CDS newest release
items.excerpt: Cognitive Design Systems' AI engineering software adds automated Design of Experiments and a Design Explorer: it sweeps parameter ranges, generates each variant and scores it on structural, manufacturing, cost and CO2 criteria.
items.rationale: New version release adding automated design-of-experiments and multi-criteria variant scoring — covers the CAD/product-design side of the section.

items.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
items.excerpt: Claude Artifacts can now be installed as beta desktop apps on Mac and Windows, even with a free account; built in chat without code, they can use OS APIs and connectors to add menu bar items, notifications and transparent windows.
items.rationale: New product release that lets designers ship chat-built prototypes as installable desktop apps with native OS surfaces (menu bar, notifications, transparent windows) — a concrete new prototyping/delivery path, no code required.
